text: I'll start at the Deployment named in the page.

remediation.name: storefront
remediation.required_value: an image reference that resolves in the registry, e.g. the last known-good published storefront tag (registry.k8s.io/retail/storefront:<existing tag>)

arguments.root_cause_statement: The new storefront release set the Deployment web/storefront pod template image to registry.k8s.io/retail/storefront:2.4.1, a reference that does not exist in the registry. Both pods of ReplicaSet storefront-68b686c56f schedule successfully onto incident-lab-control-plane but the kubelet's pull fails with "not found" (NotFound from the registry resolve step), so the containers stay in Waiting with ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff, never start, and the Deployment reports 0/2 Ready. Nothing else in the namespace is broken: the ServiceAccount, projected kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap and node capacity all resolve fine. Fix by editing the Deployment pod template image to a tag that actually exists in the repository (or rolling back to the previous release image); deleting the pods will not help because the ReplicaSet recreates them from the same template.
arguments.mechanism: The Deployment web/storefront has .spec.template.spec.containers[storefront].image set to "registry.k8s.io/retail/storefront:2.4.1", a tag that does not exist in the registry instead of a published tag, so the kubelet's pull is rejected with "not found" and both replicas sit in Waiting with ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff while the kubelet keeps re-pulling on back-off, leaving the Deployment at 0/2 Ready.

evidence.claim: The Deployment reports 0/2 Ready and both of its pods are Pending with image-pull waiting reasons.
Both pods are stuck in ImagePullBackOff / ErrImagePull.
The kubelet cannot resolve the image reference; the registry returns not found.
evidence.quote: Failed to pull image "registry.k8s.io/retail/storefront:2.4.1": rpc error: code = NotFound desc = failed to pull and unpack image "registry.k8s.io/retail/storefront:2.4.1": failed to resolve reference "registry.k8s.io/retail/storefront:2.4.1": registry.k8s.io/retail/storefront:2.4.1: not found

evidence.claim: The failure repeats for both replicas of the ReplicaSet, so it is template-driven, not pod-specific.
evidence.quote: web Warning Failed pod/storefront-68b686c56f-c7tvt x1 Failed to pull image "registry.k8s.io/retail/storefront:2.4.1"

evidence.claim: The Deployment pod template carries the unresolvable image tag, which is the object a human must edit.
The only ReplicaSet (revision 1) reproduces the same image from the Deployment template, so recreating pods cannot fix it.

ruled_out.alternative: Pods cannot be scheduled (insufficient capacity, taints, or node not ready)
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pods were scheduled onto the node successfully and PodScheduled is True; the node is Ready with full allocatable capacity.
ruled_out.quote: Normal   Scheduled  16s               default-scheduler  Successfully assigned web/storefront-68b686c56f-d4pp7 to incident-lab-control-plane

ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pull error is a NotFound on reference resolution, not an unauthorized/authentication error, and the pod spec declares no imagePullSecrets.
ruled_out.quote: code = NotFound desc = failed to pull and unpack image

ruled_out.alternative: A missing ConfigMap, Secret or ServiceAccount reference blocks the pod
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The only volume is the default projected service account token referencing kube-root-ca.crt, which exists in the namespace, and the pod is Initialized with containers only waiting on the image pull.

ruled_out.alternative: Container crashes after start (bad command, failing probe)
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The container never started: no container ID, zero restarts, state Waiting.
